label: rem:operational-entropy-properties
title: Hausdorff dimension, self-consistency, and regimes of $\eta_q$
html:
The operational entropy \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 (operational entropy) connects to the Hausdorff dimension, exhibits a forced self-consistency, and organizes the physical regimes.

Derivation from the Manning--McCluskey formula. The Manning--McCluskey formula d_H = \eta_q / \chi_q relates the Hausdorff dimension of the Julia set to the operational entropy, where \chi_q is the Lyapunov exponent. In the q-deformed Reeb dynamics, we replace the classical Lyapunov exponent \chi = \ln 2 (valid at c = 0, where the Julia set is the unit circle) with the q-deformed exponent:

  \chi_q =  \frac{1}{2q - 1}.

The substitution \ln 2 \to 1/(2q-1) reflects that the framework operates in q-deformed information units, not classical nats. The degree-2 map f_q has an effective multiplier of 1/(2q-1) in the q-connection frame. At q = 1, we recover \chi_1 = 1, meaning one nat per operation, which matches the unit-circle dynamics.

The q-deformed Hausdorff dimension of the Julia set is:

  d_{H,q} := \frac{\eta_q}{\chi_q} = \eta_q (2q - 1) = \frac{(2q - 1)^2}{q^3}.

d_{H,q} versus d_H. The formula d_{H,q} = (2q-1)^2/q^3 is exact within the q-deformed framework. It is not an approximation of the classical Hausdorff dimension d_H over \mathbb{C}. The two quantities use different Manning--McCluskey inputs:

Classical d_H q-deformed d_{H,q}
Topological entropy h_{\mathrm{top}} = \ln 2 (degree-2 map) \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 (operational entropy)
Lyapunov exponent \chi(c) (computed numerically) \chi_q = 1/(2q-1) (rational in q)
Formula d_H = \ln 2 / \chi(c) d_{H,q} = \eta_q / \chi_q
At q = 1 d_H = \ln 2 / \ln 2 = 1 d_{H,q} = 1/1 = 1
At q = q_0 d_H \approx 1.047 (transfer operator) d_{H,q} \approx 1.088 (exact)
Field dependence \mathbb{C} only Any field k with q \in k^\times

The classical d_H depends on the transcendental quantity \ln 2 and requires the analytic structure of \mathbb{C}. The q-deformed d_{H,q} is a rational function of q. It applies over any field, including \mathbb{F}_p or \mathbb{Q}_p. The two dimensions agree at q = 1 and at q = \varphi^2, but diverge elsewhere. The 3.9\% difference at q = q_0 is structural: classical conformal dynamics uses \ln 2 for the topological entropy, whereas the q-deformed dynamics uses \eta_q. We propose that d_{H,q}, rather than d_H, governs the physics.

Gravitational self-consistency forces this formula, without fitting (operational entropy is forced by self-consistency).

Physical interpretation. Each iteration of f_q corresponds to one application of the q-connection \nabla_q across a fibre (Reeb operations per Planck unit). The operational entropy \eta_q measures the information generated per iteration, representing the number of distinguishable q-bits produced by one R-matrix evaluation. The total information processed per Planck time is:

  I_P(q) = n_R(q) \eta_q = \frac{\eta_q}{\hbar_q} = \frac{2q-1}{q^2(q-1)},

where n_R(q) = 1/\hbar_q is the iteration count per Planck circuit (Planck time).

Regime behaviour.

Regime q \eta_q d_{H,q} Interpretation
Classical limit q \to 1 \to 1 \to 1 One nat per step; Julia set = unit circle
Our universe q_0 0.892 1.088 Moderate: each of {\sim}10 steps generates 0.89 q-bits
Deep quantum \varphi^2 0.327 1.000 d_{H,q} returns to 1 at the golden threshold
Deep-quantum q \to \infty \to 0 \to 0 Zero information per step; Julia set collapses

The golden crossover. The formula d_{H,q} = (2q-1)^2/q^3 equals 1 at exactly two points: q = 1 and q = (3 + \sqrt{5})/2 = \varphi^2 \approx 2.618, where \varphi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2 is the golden ratio. For 1 < q < \varphi^2, the Julia set is strictly more fractal than a circle (d_{H,q} > 1). Beyond \varphi^2, the Julia set is less complex than a circle (d_{H,q} < 1, tending toward a finite point set). This golden crossover coincides with the golden threshold (golden ratio degeneration), where the Siegel disk boundary has maximal fractal complexity.
